message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | Key Rights | How to Exercise Them | |------|------------|----------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after lease ends, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a written receipt of the deposit.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if you disagree. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain the premises in a safe, sanitary condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, etc.).
• Must comply with all building, health, and safety codes. | • Report problems in writing (email or certified mail).
• If unresolved, you may file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or seek a court order. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on how much rent can increase, but it must be in writing and given **at least 30 days’ notice** for month‑to‑month leases. | • Review your lease for any rent‑increase clauses.
• If you’re on a fixed‑term lease, increases are only allowed at the end of the term. | | **Lease Termination** | • **Month‑to‑month**: Either party may terminate with **30 days’ written notice**.
• **Fixed‑term**: Must honor the lease unless both parties agree to terminate early. | • Provide written notice (email or certified mail).
• Keep copies of all correspondence. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot disturb your peaceful use of the property. | • Document any disturbances (dates, times, nature). | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, but only after giving written notice and a reasonable time to fix. | • Keep receipts and document the issue. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide a **30‑day notice** for nonpayment of rent.
• For other reasons (lease violation, no‑fault eviction), a **60‑day notice** is required.
• Eviction must go through the court; landlords cannot forcibly remove tenants. | • Respond promptly to notices.
• Seek legal counsel if you receive an eviction notice. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR) if you suspect discrimination. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of any entries. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide a written statement of utility responsibilities. | • Verify who pays for utilities in the lease. | | **Subletting** | • Tenants may sublet only with landlord’s written consent, unless the lease prohibits it. | • Obtain written permission before subletting. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlord must keep common areas clean and safe. | • Report issues in writing. | | **Legal Remedies** | • You can sue for unpaid rent, damages, or breach of lease. | • Keep all documentation (receipts, emails, photos). | #### Quick Tips 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – It often contains specific rules that override general statutes. 2. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, emails, and written notices are your best evidence. 3. **Know the Timeline** – Notice periods and deadlines are strict; missing them can cost you. 4. **Seek Legal Help Early** – If you’re unsure about a notice or a landlord’s claim, consult a tenant‑rights attorney or a local tenant advocacy group. #### Resources - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** – [https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us](https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR)** – [https://www.tchr.texas.gov](https://www.tchr.texas.gov) - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – [https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov) - **Local Tenant Advocacy Groups** – Search for “tenant rights Texas” in your city for local support. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is general in nature and not legal advice. For specific legal questions, consult a licensed attorney in Texas.
